details: For every finite binary class, its one-inclusion average degree is at most its effective range.
proof: Every vertex of the 1-inclusion graph has degree at most \mathrm E(\mathcal H), since at most one neighbor can use each effective coordinate. Averaging the vertex degrees gives \mathrm{dens}(\mathcal H)\leq\mathrm E(\mathcal H).
name: Effective Range / Double Density or Average Degree
